items.title_original: 국방부, 첫 번째 「국방 AX 거점」 개소식 개최
items.summary: South Korea's Ministry of National Defense reported opening the first of five planned defense AI transformation hubs on October 12, at Pangyo, with a focus on physical AI research and military-civilian experimentation. The ministry described four other hubs, their institutional partners and intended work as future plans, not facilities already opened or systems deployed.
caveats: Only the Army Pangyo location is reported opened; Yongsan, Daejeon, Busan and Yangjae hubs are planned, not four additional completed openings.
Robotics, command-and-control AI, hazardous-material transport and other applications are stated future research goals, not proven operational military capabilities.
This is a Korean defense ministry press release republished by Korea Policy Briefing; independent field evidence, photo rights and source reuse approval remain unestablished.

items.title_original: 국방부차관, 방일 및 한일 국방차관회담 실시
items.summary: The South Korean defense ministry reported that Vice Minister Lee Doo-hee visited Japan on October 8–9 for meetings with Japanese defense officials, including talks with Vice-Minister Atsushi Ando, where they reaffirmed consultation on North Korea's nuclear and missile threats. They also discussed future defense exchanges involving AI and unmanned systems, without reporting a signed technology agreement.
caveats: The underlying Korean press document was distributed October 9, while its Korea Policy Briefing republication is dated October 12; the talks themselves occurred October 8–9.
The ministry's description of consultation and future collaboration does not establish a signed defense technology agreement, a program launch or joint deployment.
All assertions are attributable to this one Korean government press account and do not independently validate Japanese participation, activity or source/media reuse rights.

items.issuer: Republic of Korea Ministry of National Defense
items.summary: South Korea's defense ministry reported that the defense minister visited the Air Force's 1st Fighter Wing at Gwangju on October 14, inspecting readiness and sites associated with prospective military-airfield relocation and a national strategic-industrial project. The ministry described instructions to sustain air-defense readiness while supporting future relocation work, not a completed transfer of the air base.
caveats: The government press account reports the visit and the minister's instructions; it does not provide independent readiness-testing results or prove an operational capability improvement.
References to planned industrial-site use and airfield relocation must not be rewritten as evidence that the installation has moved, the base has been handed over or construction finished.
The ministry's account is a single institutional source; the precise site, economic implications, photographs and rights require separate verification before publication.
